slot.brief: Evaluate a definite integral like ∫ x·(inverse trig or log) dx over a simple interval using ILATE order by parts.

verdicts.working: Integration by parts gives \(\frac{x^2}{2}\arctan x-\frac12(x-\arctan x)\), evaluated from 0 to \(\sqrt3\): \(\frac{2\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\).

working:
$I=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\arctan x\right]_0^{\sqrt{3}}-\dfrac12\int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx$; $I=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac12\left(\sqrt{3}-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

Independent check: Integration by parts gives \(\frac{x^2}{2}\arctan x-\frac12(x-\arctan x)\), evaluated from 0 to \(\sqrt3\): \(\frac{2\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\).

draft.distractor_notes: A: omits the boundary contribution from integration by parts; B: forgets the factor $\dfrac12$ on the remaining integral; D: makes a sign error in the remaining integral.
